# Deep Research Intelligence Packet

## Cycle metadata

- Packet ID: `dr-20260920-0706-candidate-validation`
- Research system: `Codex web research`
- Started at: `2026-09-20 07:06 CDT`
- Completed at: `2026-09-20 07:07 CDT`
- Research scope: Validate four unresolved candidate pages for McDonald's and Taco Bell.
- Queue item or vendor: Coates Group, PAR OPS, and Restaurant365 candidate evidence.
- Methodology: Direct-page candidate validation using vendor-owned case studies; claims remain review-first and scoped to the geography or franchise operator named by the source.

## Executive result

- Pages reviewed: 4
- Candidate pages validated: 4
- Brand-vendor-product observations added or revised: 4
- Conflicts found: 0
- Material takeaway: All four candidates support real relationships, but only at the stated scope. Coates supports McDonald's Australia and New Zealand deployments. PAR OPS and Restaurant365 support named franchise operators; neither is evidence of an enterprise-wide Taco Bell, KFC, or A&W standard.

## Evidence observations

### Observation 1

- Brand: McDonald's
- Vendor: Coates Group
- Product or category: Outdoor and indoor digital menu boards, order-confirmation screens, self-service kiosks, and supporting software/integration
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: regional
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: Vendor-owned case study names the customer, products, geography, deployment counts, POS integration, and measured result. The page does not show a publication date.
- Source title: Digital Signage Improves Order Accuracy By 15% for McDonald's ANZ
- Source URL: https://coatesgroup.com/case-studies/mcdonalds-anz-digital-signage-for-order-accuracy
- Publisher or source owner: Coates Group
- Published date, if known: Not shown on page
- Accessed date: 2026-09-20
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Coates reports outdoor menu boards and confirmation screens at more than 800 locations, plus indoor menu boards and kiosks at more than 1,000 McDonald's ANZ storefronts.
- Product-specific evidence: Coates says it integrated the technology with McDonald's existing POS and reports a 15% improvement in order accuracy.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: Vendor-authored; geographic scope is Australia and New Zealand and must not be generalized globally. The page does not establish current rollout status outside the described deployment.
- Recommended follow-up: Seek a McDonald's ANZ or independent source confirming the deployment and timeframe.

### Observation 2

- Brand: McDonald's
- Vendor: Coates Group
- Product or category: Traditional building, pylon, and drive-through signage
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: regional
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: Vendor-owned case study describes a long-running named relationship, product categories, geography, and deployment counts, and explicitly says delivery continues.
- Source title: McDonald's ANZ and Coates Group Celebrate 50 Years of Partnership
- Source URL: https://coatesgroup.com/case-studies/mcdonalds-anz-and-coates-50-years-of-signage-solutions-partnership
- Publisher or source owner: Coates Group
- Published date, if known: Not shown on page
- Accessed date: 2026-09-20
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Coates describes more than 50 years supplying McDonald's ANZ and reports next-generation building signage at 250+ restaurants, pylon signs at 300+, and drive-through signage at 500+ locations.
- Product-specific evidence: The page distinguishes traditional signage packages from Coates' digital signage products and states that traditional-signage delivery continues.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: Vendor-authored and limited to Australia and New Zealand; it should not be represented as a global McDonald's technology standard.
- Recommended follow-up: Identify a dated McDonald's ANZ procurement, design-standard, or supplier-recognition source.

### Observation 3

- Brand: Taco Bell
- Vendor: PAR Technology / PAR OPS (Delaget lineage)
- Product or category: Operational analytics and reporting dashboard; DailyPay is a separate co-deployed earned-wage-access product
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: franchisee
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: PAR's case study names MAS Restaurant Group, its Taco Bell franchise scope, the number of stores, products used, and operational outcomes.
- Source title: MAS Restaurant Group partners with PAR OPS and DailyPay to improve retention
- Source URL: https://partech.com/resource/mas-taco-bell-case-study-delaget-and-dailypay/
- Publisher or source owner: PAR Technology
- Published date, if known: Not shown on page
- Accessed date: 2026-09-20
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: PAR identifies MAS as a 111-location Taco Bell franchisee in two states and says PAR OPS unified reporting across 75 existing and 36 acquired stores.
- Product-specific evidence: PAR OPS aggregates speed-of-service, sales, back-of-house, and POS data in one dashboard; the page also identifies its Coach software and DailyPay as distinct products.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: This is a franchisee deployment and is not evidence that Taco Bell corporate standardized PAR OPS or DailyPay enterprise-wide.
- Recommended follow-up: Look for MAS or Yum! Brands confirmation and a dated source establishing deployment timing.

### Observation 4

- Brand: Taco Bell; KFC; A&W
- Vendor: Restaurant365
- Product or category: Accounting and inventory platform with POS, vendor, and bank integrations
- Relationship indication: customer
- Deployment scope: franchisee
- Evidence type: case study
- Confidence: 95%
- Confidence rationale: Restaurant365's case study names BLCO Enterprises, the three franchised brands, the location count, the products used, implementation detail, and reported results.
- Source title: Smooth Roll Out of R365 at BLCO's 29 KFC, Taco Bell and A&W Locations Kicks Off Efficiency Gains
- Source URL: https://www.restaurant365.com/case-studies/smooth-roll-out-of-restaurant365-at-blcos-29-kfc-taco-bell-and-aw-locations-kicks-off-efficiency-gains/
- Publisher or source owner: Restaurant365
- Published date, if known: Not shown on page
- Accessed date: 2026-09-20
- Exact supporting excerpt or faithful factual note: Restaurant365 says BLCO operates KFC, Taco Bell, and A&W franchises and had 29 active locations on R365 after an initial four-restaurant implementation.
- Product-specific evidence: The page labels Accounting and Inventory as products used and describes integrations with POS systems, food-and-beverage vendors, and banks.
- Conflicting or limiting evidence: The page does not allocate the 29 locations by brand. This is BLCO franchisee evidence, not a corporate standard for any of the three brands.
- Recommended follow-up: Confirm BLCO's current brand/location mix and seek corporate or additional franchisee corroboration.

## Negative findings

- Candidate or claim: Enterprise-wide or global deployment inference from the four pages.
- Pages checked: All four source pages in the ledger.
- Result: None of the pages supports an enterprise-wide global standard. Each source is limited to McDonald's ANZ or a named franchise operator.

## Source ledger

| URL | Source type | Accessed | Supports observation(s) | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| https://coatesgroup.com/case-studies/mcdonalds-anz-digital-signage-for-order-accuracy | Case study | 2026-09-20 | Observation 1 | Product, geography, deployment counts, integration, and outcome stated; no page date shown. |
| https://coatesgroup.com/case-studies/mcdonalds-anz-and-coates-50-years-of-signage-solutions-partnership | Case study | 2026-09-20 | Observation 2 | Long-running ANZ relationship and product-specific counts; no page date shown. |
| https://partech.com/resource/mas-taco-bell-case-study-delaget-and-dailypay/ | Case study | 2026-09-20 | Observation 3 | Strong franchisee-level evidence; no Taco Bell enterprise claim. |
| https://www.restaurant365.com/case-studies/smooth-roll-out-of-restaurant365-at-blcos-29-kfc-taco-bell-and-aw-locations-kicks-off-efficiency-gains/ | Case study | 2026-09-20 | Observation 4 | Strong BLCO-level evidence; locations are not split by brand. |

## Research notes and inferences

- Inference: Coates appears to be a significant McDonald's ANZ signage and digital-experience supplier, but the pages alone do not establish the full current product footprint or any global mandate.
- Inference: PAR OPS and Restaurant365 have credible traction among major-brand franchisees. Franchisee adoption is marketplace evidence, not proof of franchisor selection.
- Review instruction: Preserve the exact geography/operator scope and the absence of visible publication dates during morning-cycle triage.
